title: Edges and triangles present the homotopy category of a quasicategory
statement: Use quasicategories, simplicial sets, standard simplices and edges as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a simplicial set $Q$, let $hQ$ be the category with vertices of $Q$ as objects, generated by the edges of $Q$, imposing that each degenerate edge is an identity and that every $2$-simplex with successive edges $u:x\to y$, $v:y\to z$ and long edge $w:x\to z$ imposes $[v]\circ[u]=[w]$. Here $[u]$ denotes the morphism represented by an edge. If $Q$ is a quasicategory, every morphism of $hQ$ is represented by a single edge of $Q$. Moreover, for any three edges $u:x\to y$, $v:y\to z$, $w:x\to z$, there exists a $2$-simplex with exactly these successive and long edges if and only if $[v]\circ[u]=[w]$ in $hQ$.

source.place: Cisinski, paragraphs 1.6.1 and 1.6.5, Lemmas 1.6.2 and 1.6.4, Theorem 1.6.6 (Boardman-Vogt; printed pp.21-25). The theorem identifies the edge-quotient category with the category generated by edges and triangle relations; its proof makes the existence of a composition triangle depend only on the three edge classes. Revision July 30, 2026, read directly in the online PDF and a private sandbox text extraction on 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag states this result. WANTED: archived source in literature/.

from.place: Proof paragraph 2, displayed derived R Hom / R lim calculation: coherent diagram realization through finite-Reedy localization, at the source-attachment join/cone comparison. Legitimate ordinary pullback of the cone comparison over a varying joint endpoint base. Identification of Joyal fibrations and weak equivalences between quasicategories, used to factor the graph of the comparison. At this identification, single-edge representatives and triangle realization convert isomorphisms in hFun into the actual coherent equivalence edges required by the weak-equivalence clause.
